contentEn:
Choosing a bathroom vanity and faucet feels like a design decision, but two of the three choices homeowners most often regret are functional — the size you can actually fit, and whether the faucet finish survives Vancouver's water. The third is the countertop material. Reno Stars has completed bathroom renovations across Burnaby, Richmond, Delta, North Vancouver, and West Vancouver in 2026. This guide shares what the real projects taught us.

What vanity width fits your bathroom?

The most common sizing mistake is buying a vanity based on the look before measuring the actual clearance. In a typical Vancouver condo or townhouse bathroom, you need a minimum of 90 cm (36 inches) of floor space in front of the vanity to open drawers and stand comfortably. Standard vanity widths in Canadian home centres run 60 cm, 90 cm, 120 cm, and 150 cm.

  • 60 cm (24 in): powder room or tight secondary bath
  • 90 cm (36 in): master bath baseline — fits a single sink plus storage
  • 120 cm (48 in): double-sink master bath, requires 150 cm vanity cabinet
  • 150 cm (60 in): luxury master bath, needs sufficient wall length for two mirrors

In a Richmond daughter's bathroom Reno Stars renovated with gray tiles and black fixtures, a 90 cm vanity was the maximum that allowed the shower door to open fully. In a three-and-a-half bathroom Delta townhouse renovation that took 6–8 weeks, the homeowners chose a 120 cm double-vanity and removed a recessed medicine cabinet to gain the wall space.

Which faucet finish lasts in Vancouver water?

Vancouver's water supply is classified as moderately hard to hard, depending on your municipality. Hard water leaves mineral deposits on faucet finishes faster in areas with older pipe infrastructure. The finish you choose affects both appearance and maintenance frequency.

  • Chrome: Most affordable, easiest to clean, but shows water spots within days in hard-water areas of Burnaby and Coquitlam.
  • Brushed nickel: Hides water spots better than chrome; widely available in Vancouver home centres. Lifespan 10–15 years with normal maintenance.
  • Matte black: Increasingly popular in Metro Vancouver bathrooms. Shows dust and drywall mud more than water spots. Used in the North Vancouver curbless shower project with black fixtures throughout. Requires monthly cleaning with a soft cloth only — abrasive cleaners scratch the coating.
  • Champagne gold: A premium finish that reads as warm in Vancouver's overcast winters. Requires annual sealing to maintain the coating. Seen in a West Vancouver full bathroom renovation where it was paired with cream marble wall tiles and frameless glass. Budget $350–$600 per faucet for this finish tier.

In the West Vancouver bathroom renovation, the homeowners kept the original soaker tub but had the surrounding walls re-tiled in cream marble. The champagne gold freestanding faucet and grab bar became the room's focal point. Reno Stars completed that project in 3–4 weeks.

Vanity cabinet material: solid wood vs. MDF vs. plywood

Vancouver's climate varies significantly by neighbourhood. West Vancouver and North Vancouver homes near the mountains experience higher humidity swings than Richmond or Delta, which are affected by river delta moisture. Cabinet construction matters differently depending on your area.

  • Solid wood: Most durable, resists physical damage, and accepts refinishing. In a Burnaby two-bathroom renovation Reno Stars completed in 4–5 weeks, the homeowners chose solid-wood shaker cabinets in a white finish. The cabinets survived a construction dust storm from the adjacent kitchen renovation with no swelling.
  • Plywood (exterior-grade): Used by premium Vancouver renovators as a solid-wood alternative. Handles humidity well. Acceptable in any Metro Vancouver municipality.
  • MDF (medium-density fibreboard): Budget option. Swells visibly if water reaches the seams — a real risk in families with young children. Not recommended for master bathroom vanities in Vancouver.

The Vancouver custom whole-house renovation included a master bathroom with solid-wood custom cabinetry that was built on-site to fit a non-standard alcove. Reno Stars managed that whole-house project in 3–4 weeks for the bathroom phase alone.

Countertop material: quartz vs. granite vs. laminate

Bathroom vanities sit directly above water sources, receive daily condensation from towels, and in Metro Vancouver homes may also be exposed to humidity from open windows. The countertop material you choose determines how much ongoing sealing maintenance is required.

  • Quartz: The most practical choice for Vancouver bathrooms. Non-porous, requires no sealing, resists staining from toothpaste and hair products. Available in white, gray, and concrete-look finishes that match Vancouver's contemporary renovation aesthetic. Budget $55–$120 per square foot installed.
  • Granite: Requires annual sealing. Porous surface absorbs toothpaste and cosmetics if not maintained. In the Delta townhouse renovation, granite was used on the primary bathroom countertop and the homeowners reported no issues over 18 months.
  • Laminate: Budget-friendly at $15–$35 per square foot installed. Shows seams, can delaminate near sinks over time, and has a shorter lifespan than stone. Acceptable for guest bathrooms or rental property renovations.

ADA-compliant and aging-in-place vanity choices

Vancouver's population is aging alongside the rest of BC. If you are renovating a bathroom for a parent who plans to stay in the home long-term, or you are the homeowner who intends to age in place, vanity height and clearance matter.

  • Raised toilet seats (43–46 cm bowl height) pair with a vanity at 81–86 cm for accessible reach.
  • A curbless shower — which Reno Stars installed in a North Vancouver luxury bathroom renovation — removes the threshold barrier entirely and is considered best practice for aging-in-place bathroom design in BC.
  • Pendant-accessible faucets with lever handles are easier for arthritic hands than cross handles or knob-style faucets.
  • Vancouver homeowners aged 55+ may qualify for the BC Rebate for Accessible Home Renovation (RENO) program — contact a Reno Stars project consultant to confirm eligibility before signing a renovation contract.

Layout: single vanity vs. double vanity vs. floating vanity

The choice between a single and double vanity depends on how the bathroom is used in practice. In a North Vancouver bathroom Reno Stars renovated with black fixtures and textured tile, a single floating vanity freed up floor space that made the room feel twice as large. In a Richmond bathroom renovation with gray tile and black fixtures, the homeowners opted for a single 90 cm vanity to preserve shower space.

  • Single vanity (90 cm): Works in bathrooms under 5 square metres, powder rooms, and secondary baths used by children or guests.
  • Double vanity (120–150 cm): Appropriate for master bathrooms used by two adults simultaneously. Requires a bathroom at least 7 square metres to maintain circulation.
  • Floating vanity: Elevates the cabinet off the floor, creating visual openness and making cleaning the floor easier. Cannot be wall-mounted in Vancouver condos without confirming the wall is structural or using blocking in a solid-wall renovation.

See the Delta townhouse three-and-a-half bathroom project and the North Vancouver curbless shower project for real examples of how vanity choices shaped the final bathroom design.

Frequently Asked Questions

What vanity width works in a Vancouver condo bathroom?

A 60 cm vanity fits most Vancouver condo secondary bathrooms. For a master bath, a 90 cm vanity is the minimum comfortable size. Measure the wall length and the clear floor space — you need at least 90 cm of open floor in front of the vanity to open drawers and stand comfortably.

Does Vancouver's hard water affect faucet finishes?

Yes. Hard water areas in Burnaby, Coquitlam, and parts of Surrey accelerate mineral deposit buildup on chrome and polished nickel. Brushed nickel, matte black, and champagne gold finishes hide water spots better. Installing a water softener also extends the life of any faucet finish.

How long does a bathroom vanity installation take?

A vanity-only swap — replacing the cabinet and faucet without moving plumbing — takes one to two days. If plumbing needs to be moved, budget three to five days. Reno Stars completed a two-bathroom renovation in Burnaby in 4–5 weeks; the vanity and all fixtures were installed in the second week.

What is the best countertop material for a Vancouver bathroom?

Quartz is the best all-round choice for Vancouver bathrooms. It does not require sealing, resists Vancouver's hard water staining, and holds up to daily condensation from towels and toiletries. Budget $55–$120 per square foot installed for a quality quartz countertop from a Metro Vancouver supplier.

How do I choose between a single and double vanity?

Choose a double vanity (120 cm or wider) if two adults use the bathroom simultaneously and the room is at least 7 square metres. Choose a single vanity (90 cm) in secondary bathrooms, powder rooms, or when you need to preserve floor space for a larger shower or bathtub.

選擇浴室洗臉盆和龍頭時，設計美感只是其中一環。溫哥華屋主最常後悔的決定，往往是功能層面：龍頭款式能否抵禦溫哥華的水質，以及洗臉盆尺寸是否真能放進浴室。聚星裝修 2026 年在大溫地區完成多個浴室翻新項目，本指南分享實際案例中累積的經驗。

洗臉盆寬度：哪個尺寸適合您的浴室？

最常見的錯誤是根據外觀選洗臉盆，卻沒有先測量實際可用空間。典型溫哥華公寓或聯排別墅浴室，洗臉盆前方至少需要 90 公分（36 英寸）的地面空間，才能正常開關抽屜和站立。加拿大市面上標準洗臉盆寬度為 60 公分、90 公分、120 公分和 150 公分。

  • 60 公分（24 英寸）：化妝間或空間受限的次衛
  • 90 公分（36 英寸）：主浴基本配置，單槽加收納空間
  • 120 公分（48 英寸）：雙槽主浴，需 150 公分洗臉盆櫃體
  • 150 公分（60 英寸）：豪華主浴，需足夠牆面容納兩面鏡子

列治文一個女兒浴室翻新項目（灰瓷磚、黑色五金件），90 公分洗臉盆是浴室門能完全打開的最大寬度。Delta 三套半衛浴聯排別墅翻新項目（工期 6–8 週），業主選擇了 120 公分雙槽洗臉盆，並拆除嵌入式藥櫃以爭取牆面空間。

龍頭款式：哪種表面處理能在溫哥華水質下持久？

溫哥華供水按城市行政區不同，水質為中度至硬度，影響龍頭表面的礦物質沉積速度。龍頭表面處理的選擇不僅關乎美觀，也關乎日常清潔頻率。

  • 鍍鉻（Chrome）：價格最低、保養最簡單，但在本拿比及高貴林等硬水區域，數天內即可見水漬。
  • 拉絲鎳（Brushed Nickel）：比鍍鉻更遮蓋水漬，溫哥華五金店常見款式，正常保養下壽命可達 10–15 年。
  • 啞光黑（Matte Black）：在大溫浴室中越來越受歡迎。主要缺點是粉塵和石膏灰比水漬更明顯。需每月用軟布清潔，禁用研磨性清潔劑，否則會刮傷塗層。
  • 香檳金（Champagne Gold）：高級款式，色澤溫暖，適合溫哥華陰冷的冬季。每年需拋光以維持塗層。與奶油色大理石瓷磚及無框玻璃搭配，應用於西溫全浴室翻新項目。每支香檳金龍頭預算約 $350–$600。

西溫浴室翻新項目中，業主保留原有浴缸，牆面瓷磚換成奶油色大理石，香檳金獨立式龍頭和扶手成為房間焦點。聚星裝修該項目工期為 3–4 週。

洗臉盆櫃體材質：實木 vs. MDF vs. 夾板

溫哥華各區氣候差異明顯。西溫和北溫靠山一側濕度變化大，而列治文及 Delta 受河谷濕氣影響。櫃體構造的選擇因所在區域而異。

  • 實木：最耐用，抗物理損傷，可重新打磨拋光。聚星裝修在本拿比一個雙浴室翻新項目（工期 4–5 週）中，業主選擇白色鄉村風實木櫃體，即使相鄰廚房裝修粉塵飛揚，櫃體亦無任何膨脹。
  • 夾板（exterior-grade）：高端替代實木方案，適合溫哥華各 municipality，抗潮濕能力佳。
  • MDF（中密度纖維板）：預算選項。若邊緣滲水會明顯膨脹——有小孩的家庭風險較高。不建議用於主浴室洗臉盆。

溫哥華定制全屋翻新項目中，主浴室採用現場製作的實木定制櫃體，精準貼合非標準凹槽。僅浴室部分工期為 3–4 週。

檯面材質：石英石 vs. 花崗岩 vs. 層壓板

浴室洗臉盆檯面長期接觸水源、毛巾冷凝水，以及大溫住宅開窗時的濕氣入侵。材質選擇決定了日後保養頻率。

  • 石英石：大溫浴室最實用選擇。無毛細孔，無需密封，抗牙膏及化妝品染色。供應商備有白色、灰色和清水模紋理款式，符合溫哥華現代裝修美學。每平方英尺預算 $55–$120（含安裝）。
  • 花崗岩：需每年密封。若不保養，多孔表面會吸收牙膏及化妝品。Delta 聯排別墅主浴室採用花崗岩檯面，18 個月內無問題報告。
  • 層壓板：每平方英尺 $15–$35（含安裝），預算友好。會顯示接縫，長期使用有脫層風險，使用壽命短於石材。

無障礙及長者友善洗臉盆選擇

溫哥華與 BC 省同步老齡化。若為長期居住的父母翻新浴室，或規劃自身未來在宅老化，洗臉盆高度和通道淨空非常重要。

  • 馬桶座圈高度 43–46 公分時，洗臉盆高度 81–86 公分可保障舒適使用。
  • 無障礙淋浴（步入式、無門檻）——聚星裝修在北溫豪華浴室翻新中採用此設計，BC 省無障礙住宅翻新最佳實踐。
  • 槓桿式龍頭比十字式或旋鈕式更適合關節炎患者操作。
  • 55 歲以上溫哥華業主可能符合 BC 省「無障礙家居翻新補助」（RENO）資格，請在簽約前向聚星裝修項目顧問確認。

浴室布局：單槽 vs. 雙槽 vs. 懸掛式洗臉盆

單槽或雙槽的選擇取決於浴室的實際使用情況。北溫一個浴室翻新項目（黑色五金、質感瓷磚），業主選擇懸掛式單槽，節省地面空間，視覺上空間感倍增。列治文灰瓷磚浴室項目中，業主選擇 90 公分單槽以保留淋浴空間。

  • 單槽（90 公分）：適用於 5 平方公尺以下的浴室、化妝間及兒童/客人使用的次衛。
  • 雙槽（120–150 公分）：兩位成人同時使用且浴室至少 7 平方公尺時推薦。
  • 懸掛式：櫃體懸掛離地，視覺通透，清潔地面更容易。溫哥華公寓安裝需確認牆體是否為承重結構，或使用實心牆體預埋固定件。

查看 Delta 聯排別墅三套半衛浴項目及 北溫無障礙淋浴浴室項目，了解真實案例中洗臉盆選擇如何影響最終浴室設計。

常見問題

溫哥華公寓浴室洗臉盆寬度怎麼選？

大多數溫哥華公寓次衛適合 60 公分洗臉盆。主浴舒適最小寬度為 90 公分。先測量牆面長度及洗臉盆前方淨地面空間——至少需要 90 公分才能正常開抽屜和站立。

溫哥華硬水會影響龍頭表面嗎？

會。本拿比、高貴林及素里部分區域硬水加速礦物質沉積在鍍鉻和拋光鎳表面。啞光黑、拉絲鎳和香檳金款式更遮蓋水漬。安裝軟水機也可延長任何龍頭表面的使用壽命。

浴室洗臉盆安裝需要多長時間？

僅更換洗臉盆和龍頭（不移動管線）需要一至兩天。若需移動管線，預留三至五天。聚星裝修本拿比雙浴室翻新工期為 4–5 週，洗臉盆及所有五金件在第二週完成安裝。

溫哥華浴室最佳檯面材質是什麼？

石英石是大溫浴室性價比最高的選擇。無需密封，抗硬水染色，抗牙膏及化妝品日常染色。優質石英石檯面（含安裝）每平方英尺預算 $55–$120。

如何選擇單槽或雙槽洗臉盆？

兩位成人同時使用且浴室至少 7 平方公尺，選擇雙槽（120 公分以上）。次衛、化妝間或需保留淋浴/浴缸空間時，選擇單槽（90 公分）。
